mmaths-2015-mixer-06.title: Flip a group of 10
mmaths-2015-mixer-06.body:
Separate any 10 coins into one group, leaving 90 in the other, and flip over every coin in the group of 10.

Suppose $k$ of the 10 chosen coins were heads (you do not know $k$). The group of 90 then has $10-k$ heads. After flipping, the group of 10 has $10-k$ heads too. So both groups have the same number of heads.

**Answer:** split off 10 coins and flip them all.

mmaths-2015-mixer-09.title: Reasoning from silence
mmaths-2015-mixer-09.body:
The person in back sees the other two in the room. If those two hats match (both white or both black), he knows his own hat is the other color, because there are only two of each, and he shouts.

If he stays silent, the two hats in front of him must differ.

The second person sees the first person's hat. If the back person shouts, the second person knows his hat matches the first person's. If the back person stays silent, he knows his hat is the opposite color. Either way he can be certain, so the second person is sure to survive.

**Answer: second in line**

mmaths-2015-mixer-10.title: Parity code
mmaths-2015-mixer-10.body:
Code: the person in the back says “black” if he sees an odd number of white hats and “white” if he sees an even number. His own guess is right only by luck.

Each later person knows the parity of white hats among the 9 people in front of the back person. He sees the hats in front of him and has heard the (now correct) guesses of everyone behind him except the back person, so he can work out the parity of his own hat and says his color correctly.

So the 9 people in front are always saved. No code can guarantee the back person, who has no information about his own hat, so the minimum saved is 9.

**Answer: 9**
